$comment: Reviewed default price book for the JustOne provider, seeded into the
control plane on first deploy and never overwritten afterwards.
107 minor units = CNY 1.07, derived from the vendor figure recorded in
docs/integrations/user-search-field-notes.md: JustOneAPI bills per call at
approximately USD 0.15. It is a provisional baseline, not a contract price:
the figure is approximate, was written for the user-search endpoints, and
carries an unstated USD/CNY rate.
Once the contract price is known, change it in Admin (Data Cleaning Center
-> External Data Platforms) rather than here -- a running cluster reads its
price from the database, and editing this file has no effect on it.
MONTHLY BUDGETS: both are ceilings on traffic Hub absorbs itself -- calls
from a consumer with no wallet-backed charge. A request that reserved its
own positive customer hold is not counted against either, so these do not
cap paying customers.
They are written as CALL COUNTS, because that is what an operator actually
reasons about and what the provider actually bills. The seeder multiplies
them by the highest unit price to get the minor-unit ceiling the control
plane stores, so changing a price does not silently change how many calls
the budget buys.
They must not be 0. Zero means 'absorb nothing', which rejects every such
call with external_platform_cost_budget_exhausted -- the blocked-on-day-one
state this seed exists to prevent.
Until then the cost ledger records this baseline, so treat procurement
totals for JustOne as provisional.
unitCostMinor is in minor units of `currency` (CNY: 1 = 0.01 yuan).
Every released endpoint key needs a positive price; a missing key leaves
its whole operation blocked. `bash scripts/manage.sh ops
internal-production deploy` reports any key this file does not cover.
